answer: An agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable bond before it may claim scarce work or collect rewards. The protocol releases the bond only after the agent completes a task and passes a randomly selected audit; proven duplicate claims or fabricated results forfeit it. One person can still create many identities, but each must lock real capital, so a sybil swarm multiplies the attacker’s upfront cost and ties funds up while honest agents wander from reef to meadow. This raises the price of abuse without pretending to prove identities are unique.
